🇲🇽💉 <u>COFEPRIS Busts Fake Ozempic and Saxenda Sold Online</u>

Mexico's health regulator issued an alert on November 26: counterfeit Ozempic and Saxenda are circulating through e-commerce platforms and social media, some in prefilled pens from other labs. COFEPRIS flagged Ozempic lots PP5K617 and PP7K381 and Saxenda lot MZF3L04, none of which Novo Nordisk ever released in Mexico. It also warned against illegal sales of generic semaglutide. The weight-loss boom has a black market, and the Mexican state is tracking it lot by lot.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>PAN Threatens to Boycott 2027. Sheinbaum Reads Them the Law</u>

The PAN says it won't run in 2027 unless the plurinominal rules change, claiming Morena and allies took about 54% of the vote and 73% of the seats in 2024. Sheinbaum projected the electoral law at her morning press conference and read the formula step by step: 300 deputies are won district by district, and 200 are assigned by each party's share of the vote. The opposition wants seats split by coalition. "Except the law says it's by party." Their threat is to skip an election over a formula that is already written into the Constitution.
banner: PAN BOYCOTT THREAT: 'THE LAW SAYS PARTY'

🇲🇽🌽 <u>Veracruz Raised Farm Productivity 50% in Two Years</u>

Under Governor Rocío Nahle, Veracruz's farm ministry put nearly 80% of its budget straight into producers' hands. The result: up to 50% more productivity and 80% fewer workdays thanks to mechanization. One hundred tractors and 400 implements now work 87,791 hectares. The state also opened 363 peasant schools and seven seed banks guarding 14 native maize varieties, and handed out 4,288 egg-laying poultry modules, three times as many as in 2025 and mostly to women-led families. It is food sovereignty built farm by farm.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Inés Gómez Mont Pocketed 178 Million Pesos From Shell Companies</u>

Mexico's Attorney General's Office says the former TV host received 178,723,428 pesos between 2016 and 2018 from two fake-invoice companies, Tangamanga and Gupea. The money is tied to an alleged 2.95-billion-peso embezzlement under Peña Nieto. It's one of three arrest warrants against her and her husband, Víctor Manuel Álvarez Puga. While Mexico sends Washington a diplomatic note for deporting her to Spain instead of handing her over, the FGR's file keeps growing: 12 withdrawals from the Tangamanga account alone added up to 88.74 million pesos.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>Mexico's Farms Are Not a Bargaining Chip in the T-MEC Review</u>

Julio Berdegué, Mexico's adviser on international agrifood affairs, drew the line: Mexican agriculture will not be traded away for concessions in other industries. "It is not a bargaining chip in any way." The review covers a trade relationship nearing a trillion dollars, from cars to steel. Washington's investigation into Mexican strawberries is, in his words, the start of a protectionist policy and a red line Mexico won't let it cross. The sugar dispute was settled through dialogue, and cattle exports have resumed from Sonora and Chihuahua.

text: 🚨🇲🇽 "We have made it very clear in the relationship with the United States that the relationship is one of coordination and not of subordination." "When there is a communication like the one the DEA director made, we have to speak out (...) and it is an obligation, because we have to defend sovereignty: it is the popular mandate and it is what our Constitution says." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 27, 2026 DEA Administrator Terrance Cole announced on X a channel for people to report on the Sinaloa cartel. Asked whether Washington consulted Mexico first, Sheinbaum said the US must work in its own territory: on drug consumption and on the cartels operating there. "Who distributes the fentanyl? Who sells it? Where is that money laundered?" Mexico has seized thousands of labs, and fentanyl crossings into the US have fallen about 65%, a drop US authorities recognize. Mexico's foreign minister lodged a formal complaint with the US ambassador.

🇲🇽🌎 "It's not about reaching an agreement under any circumstance, but always defending and putting the interests of the country above everything." "If this alleged criminal is extradited, it is a decision of the security cabinet about what suits Mexico. It has to do with Mexico, not with offering the United States something." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 27, 2026 Asked whether her meeting with Donald Trump at the G20 summit at Mar-a-Lago is the last chance for a tariff deal before 2027, Sheinbaum said no: Trump still has two years in office, "and there is always dialogue." Ebrard goes to Washington next week to keep negotiating with the Commerce Department and trade representative Jamieson Greer. Mexico wants lower Section 232 tariffs on cars, steel and aluminum. Of about 90 non-tariff points, she said some US requests were rejected as matters of Mexican sovereignty. A reporter asked if handing over "El Chapo Isidro" would be a sign of cooperation: "No, it has nothing to do with it."

🔥🇲🇽 "They talk about the rule of law, and the rule of law, and the rule of law. Well, the rule of law is complying with the law." "What is the underlying problem? That Mexico changed, and the people of Mexico, in their great majority, recognize the Fourth Transformation and the benefits it has brought them." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 27, 2026 Former INE presidents José Woldenberg, Luis Carlos Ugalde, Leonardo Valdés and Lorenzo Córdova called for a consensus pick for the INE's interim president and warned of a blow to its credibility. The opposition now argues that proportional-representation seats should be assigned by coalition, not by party. Sheinbaum said the electoral law is explicit that it is by party, and that the former councillors applied it that way. She played a video of Córdova, as INE president, telling deputy Guadalupe Acosta Naranjo that the 8% cap "has always been applied to parties." If they want to change the electoral law, "wait until after the 2027 election."
